narrative.northStar: The Computational Physicist's Monograph & Lab Notebook
narrative.overview:
This design system treats technical research, numerical PDEs, and high-performance computing engineering as a cohesive monograph rather than a generic blog. Every route shares a single aligned 45rem (720px) reading column anchored by a left-aligned editorial masthead on Home, a mathematical physical-field contour signature derived from a rotating-basin M2 tidal wave solution, hairline section rules, tabular numerals, and compact monospace action pills.

Neutrals hold the full canvas and structural cadence across both light and dark modes, while deep pine and ocean heritage accents mark interactive links, selections, blockquote hairlines, primary calls to action, and analytical contour lines. We explicitly reject generic WordPress academic blog patterns such as Nick Higham's nhigham.com utility sidebar, recent-posts/archive/category widget columns, subscriber widgets, and stacked blog-card boxes.
keyCharacteristics: Left-Aligned Monograph Authority: Home opens with a left-aligned portrait-and-identity masthead, the M2 rotating-basin amphidromic contour band, a ruled Current Focus line, and a three-column audience index rather than a centered social-profile card.

Hairline-Ruled Hierarchy: Log entries, CV presentations/trainings, and publication records use 1px structural hairlines on a unified canvas (#ffffff light / #1d1e20 dark) instead of elevated card boxes.

Tabular Precision & Compact Action Pills: Dates, publication metrics, CV badges, and filter controls align with tabular-nums monospace typography and 4px-radius action pills (PDF, Code, Slides, DOI, Copy BibTeX, View BibTeX) meeting WCAG 2.1 AA contrast (>= 4.5:1).

Zero-Overhead Performance: Native system sans-serif and monospace stacks eliminate webfont network latency and layout shift (CLS === 0), while progressive <details> disclosures, CSS.highlights filtering, and local video facades keep interaction instant.

rules.name: The Heritage Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Reserve deep pine and ocean exclusively for structural rules, inline prose links, selections, primary actions, and the M2 physical-field graphic; never flood general page cards with saturated brand fills.

rules.name: The Pill Contrast Rule
rules.body: Always pair small pills, tags, and action badges with primary ink over tinted pill surfaces (or canvas ink over deep pine for primary pills) to sustain >= 4.5:1 WCAG AA contrast in both light and dark modes.

rules.name: The Control Border Rule
rules.body: Give interactive pills, inputs, and disclosure controls a visible border-control stroke (>= 3.0:1 against canvas) so buttons remain unmistakable without relying on drop shadows.

rules.name: The Unified Column Measure Rule
rules.body: Align .header-nav and .main to 45rem (720px) so mastheads, prose, tables, KaTeX blocks, ruled lists, and footer chrome share exact left and right edges on desktop.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Apply font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums across ISO Log dates, publication years/metrics, CV date badges, simulation spec pills, and table cells so numeric columns align vertically.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, ruled rows, inputs, cover frames, and play controls carry zero resting box-shadow and zero hover translate lifts; spatial separation comes strictly from 1px hairlines and calibrated whitespace.

dos: Do align all site routes inside the unified 45rem (720px) monograph column with 1px solid var(--hairline) section and row dividers.
Do use --surface-pill, --border-control, and --primary (or --accent-pine / --theme for primary actions) so every badge, pill, and button maintains >= 4.5:1 contrast in both light and dark modes.
Do keep font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on ISO dates, metrics, publication years, CV badges, and tables, and min-width: 0 on all grid/flex containers down to 320px.
Do preserve native <button>, <details>, beforeprint/@media print expansion, explicit media dimensions, and prefers-reduced-motion guards.
donts: Don't imitate Nick Higham (nhigham.com) or generic WordPress academic sites: never add a right/left utility sidebar, recent-posts/archive/category widget column, subscriber widget, or stacked card-box blog feeds.
Don't restore a centered social-profile stack on Home, eyebrow kickers above <h1> headings, resting box-shadows, transform hover lifts, "Georgia" serifs, or bounce easing (1.56).
Don't set color: var(--secondary) on pill/tag surfaces, apply max-width: 68ch inside the 45rem column, inject HTML via innerHTML, or modify themes/PaperMod/.
